This wholesome and easy-to-make dish is a staple in Turkish households, perfect for any meal. instructions.title: Prepare Lentils and Aromatics
instructions.text: Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. In a large pot, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion, carrot, and potato. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until the vegetables soften.

instructions.title: Build the Flavor Base
instructions.text: Stir in the tomato paste, dried mint, red pepper flakes, and cumin. Cook for another 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, allowing the spices to become fragrant and the tomato paste to deepen in color.

instructions.title: Combine and Simmer
instructions.text: Add the rinsed lentils to the pot, then pour in the water or vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils and vegetables are very tender.

instructions.title: Blend to Smoothness
instructions.text: Remove the pot from the heat. Using an immersion blender, carefully blend the soup directly in the pot until it is completely smooth and creamy. Alternatively, transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender and blend until smooth. Be cautious as the soup is hot.

instructions.title: Season and Adjust Consistency
instructions.text: Return the blended soup to the stove over low heat. Stir in the salt and black pepper. Taste and adjust seasonings as needed. If the soup is too thick, add a little more hot water or broth until it reaches your desired consistency.

instructions.title: Prepare the Mint Butter Topping (Nane Yagi)
instructions.text: In a small pan, melt the butter over low heat. Once melted, add the extra dried mint and red pepper flakes (if using). Sauté for about 30 seconds until the mint becomes fragrant, being careful not to burn the butter.

instructions.title: Serve Mercimek Corbasi
instructions.text: Ladle the hot Mercimek Corbasi into individual serving bowls. Drizzle a spoonful of the warm mint butter topping over each bowl. Serve immediately with a wedge of fresh lemon, which is traditionally squeezed over the soup just before eating, and crusty bread.

tips: For extra flavor, use homemade chicken or vegetable broth instead of water.
Don't skip the lemon wedge! A squeeze of fresh lemon juice brightens the soup and is a traditional Turkish touch.
If you prefer a chunkier soup, blend only half of the soup and then combine with the unblended portion.
article:
Embrace the warmth and comfort of Turkish cuisine, and you'll quickly discover a culinary treasure that has captivated hearts for centuries: Mercimek Corbasi. This vibrant, wholesome, and incredibly flavorful red lentil soup is more than just a dish; it's a staple, a hug in a bowl, and an essential part of Turkish hospitality. Whether you're seeking a nutritious lunch, a comforting dinner starter, or simply a taste of authentic Turkey, Mercimek Corbasi delivers a rich, satisfying experience that is both easy to make and deeply rewarding.

## What is Mercimek Corbasi (Turkish Red Lentil Soup)?

Mercimek Corbasi, pronounced "mer-jee-MEK chor-ba-suh," is the quintessential Turkish red lentil soup. It's renowned for its smooth, creamy texture and its delicate yet distinct flavor profile, making it one of the most beloved and widely consumed soups across Turkey. Unlike some heartier, chunkier lentil soups, Mercimek Corbasi is typically pureed to a velvety consistency, offering a comforting warmth that soothes the soul.

At its core, this soup is a celebration of simple, wholesome ingredients transformed into something extraordinary. Red lentils, the star of the show, provide a naturally creamy base and are packed with protein and fiber. These are lovingly simmered with aromatic vegetables like onions and garlic, enriched with a touch of tomato paste, and seasoned with a harmonious blend of spices. The magic truly happens with the final flourish: a drizzle of *nane yağı* (mint butter or oil), infused with dried mint and vibrant red pepper flakes, which adds a crucial layer of flavor, aroma, and visual appeal. Mercimek Corbasi is a testament to how humble ingredients, prepared with care, can create a truly iconic dish.

## Ingredients for Turkish Red Lentil Soup

Creating an authentic bowl of Mercimek Corbasi relies on a few key ingredients, each playing a vital role in building its signature taste and texture. Don't let the simplicity fool you; quality ingredients make all the difference.

*   **Red Lentils:** Approximately 1 cup (200g). These break down beautifully when cooked, creating the soup's characteristic creamy texture. Ensure they are well-rinsed.
*   **Onion:** 1 medium, finely chopped. Forms the aromatic base, adding sweetness and depth.
*   **Garlic:** 2-3 cloves, minced. Complements the onion with its pungent aroma.
*   **Tomato Paste (Salça):** 1-2 tablespoons. Provides umami, a subtle tang, and a lovely reddish hue.
*   **Olive Oil or Butter:** 2-3 tablespoons. Used for sautéing the aromatics and for the finishing mint butter.
*   **Water or Vegetable Broth:** 6-7 cups (1.5-1.75 liters). The liquid base; broth adds more flavor.
*   **Salt:** To taste. Essential for seasoning.
*   **Black Pepper:** 1/2 teaspoon, or to taste. Adds a subtle warmth.
*   **Dried Mint (Nane):** 1-2 teaspoons, divided for the soup and the finishing oil. A crucial Turkish spice that imparts a refreshing, characteristic flavor.
*   **Red Pepper Flakes (Pul Biber):** 1/2 - 1 teaspoon, or to taste, for the finishing oil. Adds a gentle heat and vibrant color.
*   **Lemon Wedges:** For serving. A squeeze of fresh lemon brightens the entire soup.

Optional additions can include a pinch of cumin for earthy notes or a small carrot/potato simmered and blended for added sweetness and thickness, though these are not always in the most traditional, simple versions.

## How to Make Mercimek Corbasi: Step-by-Step Instructions

Making Mercimek Corbasi is a straightforward process that yields incredibly delicious results. Follow these steps for a perfect bowl:

1.  **Prepare the Lentils:** Start by thoroughly rinsing your red lentils under cold running water until the water runs clear. This removes excess starch, which can make the soup cloudy. Set aside.
2.  **Sauté the Aromatics:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil or butter over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onion and sauté gently for 5-7 minutes until it softens and becomes translucent. Do not brown. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
3.  **Add Tomato Paste:** Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly. This step helps to deepen the flavor of the tomato paste and removes its raw edge.
4.  **Combine and Simmer:** Add the rinsed lentils to the pot, along with 6 cups of water or vegetable broth, 1 teaspoon of dried mint, salt, and black pepper. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are very tender and have started to break down. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
5.  **Blend to Smoothness:** Once the lentils are tender, remove the pot from the heat. Use an immersion blender directly in the pot to blend the soup until it's completely smooth and creamy. If you don't have an immersion blender, carefully transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender (be cautious with hot liquids) and blend until smooth, then return it to the pot. If the soup is too thick, add a little more hot water or broth until it reaches your desired consistency. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
6.  **Prepare the Mint Butter (Nane Yağı):** In a small pan, melt 1 tablespoon of butter (or olive oil for a vegan option) over low heat. Once melted, remove from heat and stir in 1 teaspoon of dried mint and 1/2 - 1 teaspoon of red pepper flakes (pul biber). Let it sizzle gently for about 30 seconds; be careful not to burn the spices.
7.  **Serve:** Ladle the hot Mercimek Corbasi into individual bowls. Drizzle a spoonful of the fragrant mint butter over each serving. Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges on the side for squeezing.

## Pro Tips for the Best Mercimek Corbasi

Achieving that perfect, restaurant-quality Mercimek Corbasi is easy with a few expert tips:

*   **Rinse Your Lentils Thoroughly:** This is crucial. Rinsing removes starch, which can make your soup gummy or cloudy. Keep rinsing until the water runs clear.
*   **Don't Skimp on the Sautéing:** Allow the onions to soften properly and the tomato paste to cook for a minute or two. This foundational step builds layers of flavor.
*   **Blend Until Velvety Smooth:** The signature texture of Mercimek Corbasi is its creaminess. An immersion blender makes this effortless, but a regular blender works too. Ensure there are no chunky bits left.
*   **The Power of Lemon:** A generous squeeze of fresh lemon juice at the table is non-negotiable. It brightens the soup, cuts through the richness, and elevates all the flavors. Don't add it to the whole pot, as it can curdle the soup if kept warm too long.
*   **The Nane Yağı is Key:** While the soup itself is delicious, the mint-infused butter (nane yağı) is what truly distinguishes Mercimek Corbasi. It adds an incredible aroma, a pop of color, and a final flourish of flavor that makes the soup sing. Don't skip it!
*   **Adjust Consistency:** After blending, the soup might be thicker than you prefer. Have some hot water or broth on hand to thin it out to your desired consistency.

## Serving Suggestions & Pairings

Mercimek Corbasi is incredibly versatile and can be enjoyed in various ways, reflecting its humble yet beloved status in Turkish cuisine.

Traditionally, Mercimek Corbasi is served piping hot, garnished with a generous drizzle of the vibrant *nane yağı* (mint and red pepper-infused butter or olive oil) and a fresh lemon wedge. A squeeze of lemon juice just before eating is essential, as its bright acidity perfectly balances the earthy richness of the lentils.

For a complete meal, pair it with:
*   **Crusty Bread:** A staple accompaniment. Turkish bread like *pide* or *simit* is ideal for dipping, but any good quality crusty bread will do.
*   **Side Salad:** A simple fresh salad, such as *çoban salatası* (shepherd's salad) with tomatoes, cucumbers, and onions, provides a refreshing contrast.
*   **Pickled Vegetables (Turşu):** The tangy, crunchy notes of Turkish pickles offer a delightful counterpoint to the creamy soup.
*   **Olives:** A small bowl of black or green olives can complement the flavors beautifully.

Mercimek Corbasi also makes an excellent starter course for a larger Turkish meal, preceding dishes like kebabs, pilaf, or various meat and vegetable stews. Its comforting nature makes it a perfect light lunch or a warming dinner on its own, especially during colder months.

## Variations and Dietary Substitutions

One of the beautiful aspects of Mercimek Corbasi is its adaptability, making it suitable for various dietary needs and preferences.

*   **Vegan/Vegetarian:** This soup is inherently vegan and vegetarian-friendly! Simply ensure you use vegetable broth instead of water, and use olive oil for sautéing and for the *nane yağı* instead of butter.
*   **Gluten-Free:** Red lentils are naturally gluten-free, as are all the traditional spices and ingredients. This makes Mercimek Corbasi a fantastic option for those avoiding gluten.
*   **Spicier:** If you enjoy a bit more heat, you can increase the amount of red pepper flakes (pul biber) in the *nane yağı*. For an even more intense kick, you can add a pinch of cayenne pepper or a fresh finely diced chili alongside the garlic and onion.
*   **Richer Flavor:** While traditionally simple, some home cooks might add a small chopped carrot or potato along with the lentils to simmer. These vegetables will break down and blend seamlessly, adding a subtle sweetness and extra body to the soup. If using, ensure they are cooked until very tender before blending.
*   **Smoky Notes:** A tiny pinch of smoked paprika can be added along with the tomato paste for a subtle smoky depth, though this is not traditional.
*   **Herbal Variations:** While dried mint is paramount, a sprinkle of fresh parsley or dill as a garnish can add another layer of freshness.

Mercimek Corbasi truly is a versatile and forgiving recipe, allowing you to tailor it to your taste while maintaining its comforting essence.

In conclusion, Mercimek Corbasi is more than just a red lentil soup; it's an emblem of Turkish home cooking, a dish that embodies comfort, nutrition, and incredible flavor. Its simplicity belies a depth that satisfies both the palate and the soul. Whether you're a seasoned chef or a novice in the kitchen, making this iconic Turkish soup is an experience that promises warmth, deliciousness, and a delightful journey to the heart of Turkish culinary tradition. So, gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to fall in love with the comforting embrace of Mercimek Corbasi. Afiyet Olsun (Enjoy your meal)!
